# AI Policy

AG2 Assistant is itself an AI agent, and we welcome contributors who use AI tools
— including AG2 Assistant — to help build it. With that comes a simple bar:
**you remain responsible for everything you publish** — code, tests, issue
descriptions, pull request bodies, and comments.

## Code: ownership and testing

If you used AI to generate code, make sure you understand what it does and have
run it. If your tests were also AI-generated, check that they actually exercise
the behaviour — tests written alongside the code can pass while masking a bug.

By submitting a pull request you confirm you have the right to license your
contribution under the project's [Apache 2.0](../LICENSE) license, and that it
does not include third-party material you can't relicense. AI-assisted
contributions are no exception.

## Issues, PRs, and discussion

If you open an issue, describe the problem clearly enough that a maintainer can
act on it. If AI helped you draft the description, review and edit it so it
reflects your own understanding.

If you open a pull request, be able to explain the change — in the PR body and in
response to reviewer questions. If you used AI to draft text, verify any specific
claims (file paths, behaviours, error messages) against the actual diff before
submitting. Mentioning significant AI assistance in the PR body helps reviewers
calibrate their attention.

If you share raw AI output in a comment, put it in a quote block (`>`), say what
it is, and add your own commentary explaining its relevance. Please keep such
snippets short.

## Maintainer discretion

Maintainers may close or de-prioritize PRs where the contributor cannot explain
the changes, has not tested them, or cannot engage with reviewer questions. The
bar is the same regardless of how the contribution was produced — we just need to
trust that a human stands behind it.
